text: If you are smart, you will know when to keep quiet and when to criticize.
It is better to speak up than to let anger eat away at you.
When you are wrong, admit it, and you will save yourself a lot of trouble.
If a man is unable to have sex, he can't be forced to do so; but it seems harder to force some people to do right.
People who talk too much are not well liked, but people who keep quiet are often considered wise.
Their silence may just mean they have nothing to say. Or it may mean they are waiting for the right time to speak,
and that is true wisdom. But fools who always talk about themselves are never quiet.
They are disgusting, and others who grab for power also earn our hatred.
Sometimes our troubles end up helping us, and other times, good luck turns out to be bad.
Often a gift isn't really helpful, and when some people give, they expect to be repaid twice what the gift is worth.
If you search for glory you may lose what you have, but success can come to those who had humble beginnings.
What seems to be a bargain may cost you seven times what it is worth.
People love to hear wise people speak. But fools, though polite, are still fools,
and you would be better off without gifts from them, because they will expect you to give even more in return.
A small gift, they think, gives them the right to criticize—loudly. Today, they make a loan; tomorrow, they ask for their money back. I cannot stand people like this!
Fools think they have no friends and that no one appreciates their good deeds. They invite you over for a meal but believe that you will later say bad things about them.
They deserve to be mocked, and few people will pass up the chance.
It is better to slip and fall than to suffer a slip of the tongue. And something that small can bring sudden disaster to those who are evil.
A rude person is disgusting, just like the dirty stories ignorant people tell.
Everyone ignores a proverb repeated by a fool, because fools never choose the right one.
You may be too poor to commit some sins, but you can sleep at night with a clear conscience.
Have a little self-respect and don't act like a fool, or you may risk disaster.
Broken promises turn friends into enemies, so do not make promises that you cannot keep.
The ignorant are always lying, not knowing that telling a lie leaves an ugly scar.
Liars are worse than thieves, but both are on the road to destruction.
Telling lies brings disgrace and shame that never ends.
[37]If you are wise and want to succeed, you will try to please those in power.
If you plow and plant, you will harvest a crop, and if you please the powerful, they will overlook your mistakes.
Favors and gifts keep the wise from seeing the truth and muzzle the mouths of those who criticize. *
Wisdom kept secret and wealth never used do not help anybody,
but a fool does best to keep foolishness hidden.
